featured_reviews.name: Abhishek Bhoite
featured_reviews.review_text:
The Bombay Art Society's contemporary architecture from the outside is pretty iconic, but it is in ruins from the inside. The maintenance of the gallery is below par. The staircase is a piece of art in itself.

There is a ramp at the main entrance for wheelchairs, but the restrooms inside the building are not accessible & very shabbily made.

This is an excellent example of how the architect's vision has been destroyed by the people & contractors who run the place. The gallery definitely has a lot of scope to develop in the future.
featured_reviews.response_from_owner_text:
Before writing such review, you should at least get some basic information about public art institution serving society at large and promting art and artists. We don't know what time of the year you visited but just after COVID the art galleries condition was bit of an issue due to rainwater leakage; due to leakage, some part of false ceiling was collapsed during lockdown, place was bit moist, and it took bit of a time to fix it. It is fixed long back, and all three galleries are functioning and there are regular exhibitions taking place in the galleries; not only that but community art classes also started; our auditorium is functioning. 
Washroom cleaning was small issue immediately after COVID and is taken care now, as there is ample staff. 
The structure is architecturally beautiful from outside; it is the same architect who has designed it from inside too. 
The place is run by the managing committee consisting of artists and art writers and contractor have no role after building is completed. The Bombay Art Society is one of the oldest art institutions in Asia promoting art and artists; Society is always run by committee for 135 years since 1888; committee is elected every three/five years by society's life members. This complex is new, and every new art space takes time to build its own audience. 
Please don't spread misinformation based on single visit. Hope, you will visit our art galleries when you are in the area. 
The Bombay Art Society Team

It’s surprising how many students believe that NID NIFT & UCEED are the only pathways into design.

Yet many students never learn about these options because they are only guided toward the most commonly known exams or given options with hefty fee structure. 

Every student is different. Some may thrive in product design, others in communication design, animation, fashion, architecture, UX, game design or strategic design. The best college is not always the most famous one, it’s the one that aligns with your skills, interests and career goals.

Before deciding your future, explore all the possibilities, understand the differences and make an informed choice.

Check other design entrance options and pathways.

Character Rotation: Building Real Design Skills

Character rotation is more than drawing the same character from different angles. It helps students understand form, proportion, structure, volume, and spatial visualization which are essential skills used in animation, game design, illustration and product design.

This exercise teaches students how to think in 3D and maintain consistency across every view of a character.

Good Design colleges select students based on their skills, creative thinking, observation, and problem-solving abilities, not shortcuts. 

Shortcuts may produce quick results, but they don’t build strong pedigree. A college’s pedigree is defined by the quality of its students, the rigor of its training and the achievements of its alumni.

While AI and digital tools can enhance creativity, they are most effective when built upon strong foundational skills. First develop the ability to draw, observe, visualize and design. Then use advanced tools to push your ideas even further.

I’m currently in my second year of BFA at NIFA (National Institute of Fine Arts), and the growth I’ve experienced here has been truly meaningful. In just over a year, my confidence, observation skills, and technical ability have improved in a way that reflects directly in my artworks.

I’ve trained in multiple mediums here, including fine pen, acrylic, oil paints, watercolor, charcoal, and pencil shading. The guidance from Madhu Sir and Mandar Sir has been the most valuable part of my journey. Their experience, personal attention, and honest feedback have helped me grow both technically and creatively.

Alongside regular classes, NIFA also organizes enriching workshops like the Caricature Art Workshop, which allow us to explore different art styles and techniques beyond the syllabus.

You can view my art journey and progress on Instagram: @nishantchoudhary.arts — a reflection of everything I’ve learned here.

Even as I move forward in my art career, I will always remain a student of NIFA, and of Madhu Sir and Mandar Sir. I’m thankful to be part of this institute and highly recommend it to anyone serious about building their future in fine arts.
